HELD-OUT, frozen 2026-10-23, LABELLED BEFORE THE SLOTTER WAS RUN ON IT. The 13/13 on the gold set is IN-SAMPLE: the cardinality registry was written by someone who had read those labels, so it is a fit, not a measurement. This file is drawn from the 26 real graph facts the gold set left unkeyed and from the 12 SQLite memory_facts rows -- a DIFFERENT extractor, so a different distribution. No invented cases.

Its purpose is the FALSE-POSITIVE channel, which the gold set could not test: a SLOT COLLISION, where two facts about genuinely different things both land in one declared single-valued slot. Two real instances are here (diet, identity:name) and they are the rows that matter. 10 of 12 pairs are labelled compatible or paraphrase ON PURPOSE -- this set is weighted to catch over-flagging, because an over-flag makes a true memory invisible while a miss merely leaves her inconsistent.

facts.name_ben: His name is Ben and he prefers to be called that
facts.diet_veg: Ben is vegetarian and does not eat meat
facts.diet_eggs: Ben enjoys eggs benedict and apple juice for breakfast
facts.nick_daddy: Ben likes to be called Daddy during sex
facts.hob_gaming: Ben likes gaming, especially RPGs like Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077
facts.hob_beach: Ben enjoys beach activities and reading on the beach
facts.sex_control: Ben likes to be in control during sex
facts.sex_rough: Ben likes rough, intense and primal sex
facts.sex_dom: Ben has a preference for deep-throating and being dominated
facts.goal_your: His goal is to start something of your own
facts.goal_my: His goal is to start something of my own
facts.conc_runway: He is concerned about the money runway
facts.conc_runway2: He is concerned about the money runway
facts.conc_dec: He is concerned about a decision
facts.books: Ben reads general-interest books such as Animal Farm and Jordan Peterson's 12 Rules for Life
facts.car: Ben sold his car in June or July 2026

pairs.label: compatible
pairs.why: BOTH TRUE AND BOTH PLAUSIBLY `diet`, which is DECLARED SINGLE-VALUED. Eggs are vegetarian, so these agree -- but a slotter that puts both in `diet` retires one. This is the collision channel firing on real data, and it is the single most important row in this file.

pairs.label: compatible
pairs.why: `identity:name` is declared single-valued and these ARE two values. But 'Ben' is what he prefers to be CALLED and 'Ramon' is from a different store written by a different extractor. The baseline already recorded the verdict: which is correct is the operator's call, not a detector's. A detector that retires one has destroyed the operator's own decision.

pairs.label: paraphrase
pairs.why: the SAME goal in second and first person -- an artefact of the extractor reading her turn and his turn. Must not be called a contradiction.

pairs.label: paraphrase
pairs.why: byte-identical, and BOTH LIVE in memory_facts because its supersede key could never fire. Exact containment already catches this; it is here so the new path cannot make it worse.

pairs.label: paraphrase
pairs.why: same VALUE ('Daddy') in a single-valued slot -- the value test must stop this before cardinality is consulted.

pairs.label: compatible
pairs.why: a preference about control and one about location -- different things

pairs.label: compatible
pairs.why: overlapping preferences that coexist; the store holds six of these

known_limits: One operator, two extractors. This measures generalisation across phrasings and across writers, NOT across people. And it contains no case of two simultaneously-true values in a NARROW slot (two dogs, two homes) because the operator has one of each -- that residual channel stays unmeasured and the shadow ledger is the only instrument for it.
